facts.statement: Maip lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) in the Chorrillo Formation of Santa Cruz, Argentina.
facts.quote: Maip is a genus of large megaraptorid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) Chorrillo Formation of Santa Cruz, Argentina.

facts.statement: The genus Maip contains only one known species, M. macrothorax, which is known from an incomplete and disarticulated skeleton.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, M. macrothorax, known from an incomplete, disarticulated skeleton.

facts.statement: Maip may represent the largest known megaraptorid from South America and possibly the largest in the world.
facts.quote: Maip may represent the largest megaraptorid known from South America, and possibly the world.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPM 21545 was discovered by Alexis Rolando in 2019 on the La Anita Farm, 30 km west of El Calafate, Argentina.
facts.quote: The Maip holotype specimen, MPM 21545, was discovered by Alexis Rolando on the La Anita Farm, 30 km west of El Calafate, Santa Cruz province, Argentina, in 2019.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen was found disarticulated but associated over an area measuring 5 by 3 square meters.
facts.quote: The specimen was found disarticulated but in association over an area of 5x3 m2.

facts.statement: The known fossil material includes the axis, dorsal and caudal vertebrae, ribs, gastralia, a left coracoid, a fragmentary scapula, a partial right pubis, and a partial metatarsal.
facts.quote: The known fossil material consists of the axis, several dorsal and caudal vertebrae, cervical and dorsal ribs, gastralia, a left coracoid, fragmentary scapula, partial right pubis, and partial metatarsal.

facts.statement: Maip was first announced in a 2021 preprint but was considered informally named because the paper did not meet necessary requirements.
facts.quote: Maip was first announced in a Research Square preprint in 2021. However, since the paper did not meet the necessary requirements, the taxon was considered informally named.

facts.statement: The genus and species Maip macrothorax were validly described in 2022 by Aranciaga Rolando et al.
facts.quote: In 2022, the fossil material was validly described as belonging to a new genus and species of megaraptorid by Aranciaga Rolando et al.

facts.statement: The specific name macrothorax means large chest, referring to the animal's large thoracic cavity.
facts.quote: The specific name, "macrothorax", is derived from the Greek "makrós", meaning "large", and the Latin "thorax", meaning "chest", in reference to its large thoracic cavity.

facts.statement: Maip is estimated to have been around 9 meters long and weighed over 1.3 metric tons.
facts.quote: Maip is the largest known megaraptorid, estimated to have been around 9 m long and weighed over 1.3 MT.

facts.statement: Based on ligament attachment traces on the ribs, it is inferred that Maip had a respiratory system comparable to modern birds rather than crocodilians.
facts.quote: Traces on the preserved ribs were interpreted by the describing authors as being attachment points for ligaments. From these, it was inferred that Maip would have likely had a respiratory system comparable to those of modern birds, rather than those of other extant reptiles, such as crocodilians.

facts.statement: Megaraptora is classified within Coelurosauria as the sister taxon to Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: Megaraptora is nested within Coelurosauria, as the sister taxon to Tyrannosauroidea.

facts.statement: Maip is estimated to have been between 9 and 10 meters long in life.
facts.quote: Se estima que Maip tenía alrededor de 9 a 10 metros de largo en vida.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MPM 21545 was discovered at La Anita Farm, 30 kilometers west of El Calafate, Santa Cruz province, Argentina.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo de Maip, MPM 21545, fue descubierto en la Granja La Anita, 30 kilómetros al oeste de El Calafate, provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina.

facts.statement: The known fossil material consists of the axis, dorsal and caudal vertebrae, cervical and dorsal ribs, gastralia, a left coracoid, a fragmentary scapula, a partial pubis, and a partial metatarsal.
facts.quote: El material fósil conocido consta del axis, varias vértebras dorsales y caudales, costillas cervicales y dorsales , gastralia, un coracoides izquierdo, escápula fragmentada, pubis parcial y metatarsiano parcial.

facts.statement: The specimen was found disarticulated but associated in an area of 5 by 3 square meters.
facts.quote: El espécimen se encontró desarticulado pero asociado en un área de 5 por 3 metros cuadrados.

facts.statement: Maip was first announced in a 2021 Research Square preprint but was considered informally named because the document did not meet necessary requirements.
facts.quote: Maip se anunció por primera vez en una preimpresión de Research Square en 2021. Sin embargo, dado que el documento no cumplía con los requisitos necesarios, se consideró que el nombre del taxón era informal.

facts.statement: The fossil material was validly described as a new genus and species of megaraptorid in 2022 by Rolando et al.
facts.quote: En 2022, el material fósil fue descrito válidamente como perteneciente a un nuevo género y especie de megaraptóridos por Rolando et al..

facts.statement: The generic name Maip refers to a malicious being in Aonikenk mythology known as the shadow of death that kills with cold wind.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico, Maip, hace referencia a un ser malicioso en la mitología Aonikenk que es "la sombra de la muerte que mata con viento frío".

facts.statement: The specific name M. macrotórax is derived from Greek and Latin words meaning long and chest, referring to its large thoracic cavity.
facts.quote: El nombre específico, M. macrotórax, se deriva del griego makrós, que significa "largo", y el latín tórax, que significa "pecho", en referencia a su gran cavidad torácica.

facts.statement: In 2022, Rolando et al. recovered Maip as a derived megaraptorid in a polytomy with other Argentine megaraptorids.
facts.quote: En sus análisis filogenéticos, Rolando et al. de 2022 recuperaron a Maip como un megaraptórido derivado en una politomía con otros megaraptóridos argentinos.

facts.statement: Like previous analyses, Megaraptora is nested within Coelurosauria as the sister taxon to Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: Al igual que los análisis previos de otros autores, Megaraptora se anida dentro de Coelurosauria, como el taxón hermano de Tyrannosauroidea.

facts.statement: Maip fossils are known from the Chorrillo Formation in southern Argentina, which dates to the Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Formación chorrillo Maip se conoce de la Formación Chorrillo del sur de Argentina, fechada en el Maastrichtiense.

facts.statement: Maip is classified within the family Megaraptoridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Megaraptoridae

facts.statement: Maip lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Chorrillo Formation also contains named dinosaurs such as the ornithopod Isasicursor and the sauropod Nullotitan.
facts.quote: Otros dinosaurios con nombre conocidos de la formación incluyen Isasicursor, un ornitópodo elasmariano y Nullotitan , un saurópodo titanosauriano.

facts.statement: Fragmentary fossil material including teeth and a dorsal vertebra has been assigned megaraptorid affinities but is too incomplete to be linked to Maip or any other specific taxon.
facts.quote: Material fósil muy fragmentario, incluidos los dientes y el centro dorsal, ha sido clasificado como poseedor de afinidades megaraptóridas, pero es demasiado fragmentario para ser asignado a Maip o cualquier otro taxón.
